alignments.note: Relative ὅς → 'who'.
Participle ὤν → 'being'.
Anarthrous ἀπαύγασμα → 'the effulgence'; no article competes, so the supplied determiner is a rule 7 helper on the noun (rule 51).
No genitive pronoun stands with δόξης, so the article is not displaced and is what the supplied possessive realizes: 'of his' headed on 'his', the case preposition riding along (rules 20, 21).
δόξης → 'glory'.
καί → 'and'.
χαρακτήρ → 'the very image'; 'image' glosses the lexeme and 'very' only intensifies it, so rule 66 heads the unit on 'image', the supplied determiner riding along on the anarthrous noun.
αὐτοῦ is present and free to carry the possessive, so rule 20 proper applies and this article realizes nothing.
'of … substance': with the article emptied by the possessive, the case preposition stays with the noun (rule 20), discontinuous under rule 15.
Genitive pronoun αὐτοῦ → 'his'.
Participle φέρων → 'upholding'.
Connective τε → 'and'; the ASV writes a word for it, so it is aligned rather than left empty.

Article before the substantival adjective takes the supplied nominal 'things' (rules 22, 102). Rule 17's 'all things heads on All' is scoped to anarthrous Greek; here an article stands, so the supplied noun is the article's own.
πάντα → 'all', left bare beside the article (rule 102).
Dative article with its case preposition: 'by the' headed on 'the' (rules 17, 21).
ῥήματι → 'word'.
αὐτοῦ carries the possessive, so the article is displaced (rule 20).
'of … power', the case preposition staying with the noun since the article is emptied (rule 20).
Genitive pronoun αὐτοῦ → 'his'.
καθαρισμόν → 'purification'.
The ASV gives 'sins' no determiner, so the article has no 'the' to anchor (rules 21, 23).
'of sins': with no determiner written, the case preposition stays with the noun (rule 21).

Participle ποιησάμενος recast as a finite clause: the supplied subordinator 'when', the subject and the auxiliary are all rule 7 helpers on the participle, which carries the subordination (rules 86, 88), headed on the lexical verb.
ἐκάθισεν → 'sat down'; 'down' is the English verb's own particle.
ἐν → 'on'.

Anarthrous substantival δεξιᾷ → 'the right hand'; it is the nominal word and takes the supplied determiner itself (rule 58), and rule 17's generic-noun clause heads the unit on 'right' rather than on the supplied 'hand'.
Genitive article with its case preposition: 'of the' headed on 'the' (rule 21).
μεγαλωσύνης → 'Majesty'.
ἐν → 'on'.
ὑψηλοῖς → 'high'.

review_notes: Three genitive articles were decided separately and came out differently: τῆς δόξης has no genitive pronoun and so takes the supplied 'his' (rule 20's second arm), while τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ and τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ are displaced by an expressed αὐτοῦ.

τὰ πάντα: heading the article's unit on 'things' follows rule 102 and rule 22's determiner clause. Reading it rule 17's way — 'all things' whole on πάντα headed on 'all', with τά unrepresented — remains defensible, but rule 102 scopes rule 17's generic-noun clause to anarthrous Greek and an article stands here.
Both variant units are marked selected with no FALLBACK EXCLUDED line, so rule 97 is not in question.
